title: A Systematic Review of the Effectiveness of Algebraic Teaching Interventions: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Synthesis
venue: Nordic Journal of Systematic Reviews in Education
extended_summary:
This paper presents a protocol for a systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-synthesis of algebraic teaching interventions for K-12 students. The authors ask which algebra interventions are effective, for whom, and under what conditions, motivated by the persistent difficulty students have with algebra and the importance of algebra for later mathematics and STEM success.

The planned review will synthesize empirical studies conducted in the United States from 1980 to the present, covering early algebra, pre-algebra, and algebra instruction across elementary, middle, and high school grades. The intervention category is broad: any classroom-based algebraic teaching intervention delivered by a teacher, researcher, or technology compared with business-as-usual instruction. The meta-analysis will estimate standardized mean differences and examine moderators such as grade level, algebraic big ideas, demographic variables, intervention type, delivery mode, training, publication type, and assessment type.

The meta-synthesis will qualitatively examine the characteristics of effective interventions, their learning goals, and the nature of students’ mathematical thinking. The authors argue that combining quantitative and qualitative synthesis will provide a more complete picture of algebra instruction than prior reviews and help identify best practices across grade levels and student groups. Because this is a protocol paper, it reports planned methods rather than completed results.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a protocol for a systematic review/meta-analysis rather than a completed empirical study. It describes planned methods, not analyzed evidence or results, so it does not meet the criteria for a completed meta-analysis or trial.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effects are reported, so there is no demonstrated educational impact to classify. The paper is important as a research protocol, but it provides no measurable student or institutional outcome effect.

finding.finding_summary: This paper is a systematic review/meta-analysis protocol, not a completed intervention study, so it reports no empirical effect estimate yet. It proposes to synthesize the effectiveness of algebraic teaching interventions on mathematics learning, thinking, and knowledge across Grades K-12, but provides no results, effect sizes, or sample sizes in the text provided.
finding.measure: Planned measures of mathematics learning, thinking, or knowledge; standardized mean differences (Hedges' g) from included studies

finding.finding_summary: The article’s substantive contribution is methodological and agenda-setting: it lays out a protocol for a mixed-methods evidence synthesis intended to inform policy, practice, and future research in school algebra. No empirical impact is reported because the review has not yet been conducted and no effect estimates are available.
finding.measure: Planned synthesis of intervention effects, moderators, and thematic recommendations for policy/practice
